data.name: Nylah
data.gender_notes: Nylah is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A name of unknown origin, potentially derived from Greek nyktos (night) and hele (light). In Christian symbolism, Nylah represents the light that shines in the darkest hours. The name Nylah carries the meaning “Night Light” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Nylah usually hope their child will grow to embody night light and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A beacon of hope and guidance in times of darkness.
data.etymology: Nylah belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Night Light.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Nylah total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_hebrew.name: נילה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם נילה הוא שילוב של המילים העבריות 'נ' ו'ילה', שפירושן מתנה של אלוהים לנחלה. השם קשור לנחלות האלוהיות והוא מבטא את הרעיון של מתנה אלוהית יקרה.

in_greek.name: Νύλα
in_greek.long_meaning: Τὸ ὄνομα Νύλα προέρχεται ἀπὸ τὴν ἑβραϊκὴ λέξη, ἡ ὁποία σημαίνει δωρεὰ Θεοῦ. Στὴν Καινή Διαθήκη, τὸ ὄνομα αὐτὸ ἐμφανίζεται ὡς σύμβολο τῆς χάριτος καὶ τῆς εὐλογίας τοῦ Θεοῦ.

in_latin.name: Nylah
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Nylah originem habet in voce hebraica, quae donum Dei significat. In Ecclesia primitiva, nomen hoc habebat significationem gratiae et benedictionis Domini.

in_english.name: Nylah
in_english.long_meaning: The name Nylah is derived from Hebrew roots, signifying 'Gift of God' or 'Gracious'. Although not directly mentioned in the Bible, it embodies the concept of divine favor and blessing. Historically, the name has been used across Christian cultures to signify a child born with God's grace and love. It symbolizes spiritual gifts and divine providence.

data.cultural_impact: Nylah reflects the cultural and spiritual values of the Biblical tradition and is used in Christian communities.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, Nylah is chosen for its meaning “Night Light” and the hope that the child embodies it.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Nylah: Derived from Hebrew, meaning "rest, repose, tranquility." In Christianity, it can symbolize the peaceful surrender to God's will and seeking refuge in His love and protection.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Nylah remains relevant in modern Christian society, representing a bridge between traditional Biblical values and contemporary life.
